Person.description: Someone who files or is named in a filing. Recorded once, however many cases they have.

Address.description: A place a person lives or receives mail.

Relationship.description: A family link between two people, such as spouse or child.

Case.description: One filing by one person, from intake through decision.

AsylumCase.description: A case filed by someone already in the country.

RefugeeCase.description: A case processed for someone outside the country.

Interview.description: A scheduled conversation between an officer and the person on a case.

Appeal.description: A request to review a decision on a case.

Tag.description: A label officers attach to cases to find them later.

VettingCheck.description: One security or identity check run for a case.

BiometricCheck.description: A check based on fingerprints or photos.

NameCheck.description: A check of names and dates of birth against watch lists.

Referral.description: A request to send a case to another office for review.

ReferralEvent.description: Something that happened to a referral, in order.

Note.description: A free-text note on a person or case.

Document.description: A file attached to a person, case, or check.

User.description: A staff member who works cases.

tours.name: How a case moves through the system

steps.title: Overview
steps.note: Each shaded zone is one part of the system. Lines show how records connect, and the ends of each line show one or many.

steps.title: Person
steps.note: A person is recorded once, with addresses and family relationships, however many filings they have.

steps.title: Case
steps.note: Every filing is a case. Asylum and refugee cases share one table and differ only by type.

steps.title: Vetting check
steps.note: Each case runs several checks. Biometric and name checks are kinds of vetting check.

steps.title: Referral
steps.note: When a case needs another office, a referral records who sent it, why, and every event since.
